title: Google Ads for service businesses: 10 keyword patterns that generate enquiries
excerpt: More keywords are not necessarily better; intent matters. These are search patterns with commercial intent in Montenegro and ways to group them so Google Ads attracts enquiries rather than empty clicks.
description: More keywords are not necessarily better; intent matters. These are search patterns with commercial intent in Montenegro and ways to group them so Google Ads attracts enquiries rather than empty clicks.
coverAlt: Google Search and lead-generation keywords in Montenegro
segments: Many Google campaigns for service businesses in Montenegro waste money for two reasons: targeting searches with overly broad intent or combining several services in one ad group. The result is familiar: clicks arrive but enquiries are weak or absent. Google itself is not the problem; the campaign is buying the wrong attention.

If you need enquiries, target commercial intent. These are searches from people already looking for a solution, price, contact, appointment, quotation or provider in their city. Local intent is especially strong in Montenegro, where people often want an answer immediately and nearby.
Why many Google campaigns waste spend

Campaigns often include informational terms such as how, what is, ideas or examples. You then pay for research clicks rather than prospective customers. Another mistake is mixing event organization, hostesses, audio equipment and photo/video into one campaign. The ad and landing page fail to match the search, Quality Score can suffer, CPC rises and performance declines.
The quickest improvement is to group keywords by intent instead of collecting a long list of terms. Relevance and clarity are central to Google Ads performance.
10 keyword patterns that often generate enquiries
Rather than chasing one magic keyword, use patterns. Adapt each to your service and location. These are common types of high-intent search:
1) Service + city
Examples: event organization Budva, lawyer Bar, air conditioning repair Nikšić, dentist Herceg Novi. This is classic 'I want someone nearby' intent.
2) Agency or company + city
Examples: marketing agency Montenegro, event agency Budva, accounting service Podgorica. The person is seeking a provider, not advice.
3) Price + service
Examples: event organization cost, video production price, SEO pricing. These searches can be price-sensitive but often indicate serious budget consideration.
4) Quote + service
Examples: sound equipment quote, hostess staffing quote, event production quote. These express strong commercial intent because the person is already comparing providers.
5) Best + service
Examples: best event agency, best photographer, best catering. Use carefully, but these searches can work because people look for recommendations.
6) Urgent, fast, appointment
Examples: emergency plumber, same-day cleaning, dentist appointment today. Urgency can signal strong purchase intent.
7) Hire, rental or lease
When relevant: sound system rental, lighting rental or stage rental. These indicate clear needs.
8) Specific service within a broader category
Examples: promotional hostesses, promoters or event registration staff. More specific queries often indicate stronger intent.
9) Production or organization
For events and other complex services: event production, conference organization, technical production. These users seek a capable team rather than equipment alone.
10) Contact, number or phone
Often underrated but high-intent. People add contact details or phone-related terms to searches when they are ready to call. Those queries may deliver strong leads.
How to group keywords for a better Quality Score

The principle is simple: one service per ad group and one intent per ad set. If someone searches for prices, your ads and landing page should address price ranges, not vague claims of being the best. For service + city searches, clearly state you work in that location, what you provide and how to contact you.
A common mistake is using one landing page to answer every query. A strong campaign aligns the landing content with the search intent, supporting relevance, CPC efficiency and lead quality.
Negative keywords

Without negatives, ads can show to people who are not prospective customers. Common filters include how, what is, free, course, job, PDF, template, example and ideas. If you actually sell courses or templates, those terms are not necessarily negatives. Filter according to what you offer.
Google Ads succeeds when it reaches buyers' intent rather than curiosity.
FAQ
Does broad match work?

It can, with a well-established account, reliable tracking and a strong negative keyword strategy. When starting, a more controlled approach makes it easier to see which searches generate real enquiries.
What matters most?
The ad and landing page must answer the searcher's intent closely. That improves both relevance and the quality of enquiries.
